documents.title: Claims ledger: the audit's written record
Terms acceptance: wording, links and record

claims.quote: Provisioning job logs: 30 days by default.

evidence.shows: The published default window for job logs is 30 days.
The collector reads its default window from that same constant.
The collector passes that window to the SQL function that deletes.

evidence.pattern: FUNCTION public\.gc_job_logs\(\s*p_age INTERVAL DEFAULT INTERVAL '30 days'
evidence.shows: The SQL function's own default is also 30 days.

claims.quote: Removed cloud inventory and capability observations: 7 days by default.

evidence.shows: The sweep's default window is 7 days, overridable by one environment variable.
Removed inventory rows are purged with that window.
Removed capability observations are purged with the same window.

claims.quote: {CONSENT_COOKIE_NAME}: records the analytics choice, the policy version, and the decision time for 183 days.

evidence.shows: The cookie's lifetime is 183 days.
That lifetime is what the cookie is written with.
The record holds the policy version and the decision time beside the choice.
The name the browser holds.
The name the page prints is the same string.

claims.quote: There is exactly one optional choice — product analytics — and it is off until you turn it on.

evidence.shows: The consent record carries one optional choice.
With no stored record the answer is no.
Without that answer the console does not load the analytics SDK.
The SDK itself starts opted out.

claims.quote: if your browser sends the GPC signal, optional analytics stays off and the stored choice cannot override it

evidence.shows: The signal is read before the stored choice and wins over it.
The console asks for that combined answer, not for the stored field.

claims.quote: the analytics SDK is configured so that recording cannot start.

evidence.shows: The SDK is initialised with recording disabled.

claims.quote: Paid plans are billed through Stripe, which acts as our payment processor.

evidence.shows: Stripe is in the processing register as an active party, so the subprocessors page lists it.
The console depends on the Stripe SDK.

claims.quote: The company is not registered for VAT.

evidence.shows: The entity record says the company is not registered for VAT.

claims.quote: Transactional email is delivered through Amazon Web Services (Amazon SES) in its Frankfurt, Germany region (eu-central-1).

evidence.shows: The hosted deploy sends through SES unless the vault names another transport.
The deploy refuses a vault that still names Resend.
The SES account the hosted service sends from is in eu-central-1.
The processing register records SES as active, so the subprocessors page lists it.

claims.requires: The value of EMAIL_PROVIDER in the production vault. Unset and ses both mean SES, and the deploy refuses resend; but the vault may name smtp, the rollback transport, and while it does the statement is false.

claims.quote: > I have read and accept the Terms of Service (version 2026-08-24).

evidence.shows: The label opens with the shared constant the e2e fixture locates the box by.
The module builds the label from that prefix followed by "the".
Each document title is followed by its version in brackets.
The Terms of Service are sealed at version 2026-08-24, the version the example prints.

claims.quote: > How we use your personal data is explained in our Privacy Policy.

evidence.pattern: noticeBefore: "How we use your personal data is explained in our ",
evidence.shows: The notice line opens with these words and is followed by the Privacy Policy link.
The notice line links the Privacy Policy.
The Privacy Policy is not an acceptance-required document, so the box does not cover it.

claims.quote: The accepted set is every document in `LEGAL_DOCUMENTS` with `acceptanceRequired: true`.

evidence.shows: The module derives the accepted set from the registry flag.
The server action records only acceptance-required documents.

claims.quote: The version and the hash are copied in, never looked up later.

evidence.shows: The server action writes the sealed version and hash from the registry into the row it inserts.
The module names the same two registry values for the same documents.

claims.quote: `signup` if the person never accepted any version of the document before, otherwise `reacceptance`

evidence.shows: The context is signup for a first acceptance and reacceptance otherwise.
First acceptance is decided per document from the stored rows, not from client input.

claims.quote: Submitting twice does not add a second row for the same version.

evidence.shows: An existing row for the same person, document and version skips the insert.

claims.quote: Links use the instance's legal address (`legalUrl`, which reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_LEGAL_URL`)

evidence.shows: The module resolves links through legalUrl by default.
legalUrl reads NEXT_PUBLIC_LEGAL_URL.

findings.says: The page tells the reader the Terms were last updated on August 12, 2026.
findings.actually: The sealed version is 2026-08-24: sections 5 and 13 were changed on that date and the version was bumped for it. The date on the page was not moved, so a reader who accepts version 2026-08-24 is shown a date twelve days older.

evidence.shows: The registry's version for the Terms.

findings.quote: can change analytics and replay consent immediately
findings.says: The page says a visitor can change a replay consent.
findings.actually: There is no replay consent. The consent record holds one choice, analytics; the Cookie Notice says there is no replay choice to make.

evidence.shows: The consent record has exactly one field.
The Cookie Notice says the opposite of this page.

findings.quote: You can export all of it in a machine-readable archive from the console, at any time and without asking us.
findings.says: The page says the console offers a self-service export of everything Alethia holds, with a manifest.
findings.actually: The console has no export. The manifest format exists (apps/console/lib/privacy/manifest.ts) and the privacy case table has columns for an export, but on 2026-11-17 nothing under apps/console imported the manifest module except its own test, and no server action or route builds an archive. Board unit LEG-L3 builds the export; until it lands the sentence is not true. The page's 30-day transition and retrieval windows were also searched for in apps/console/lib/privacy and apps/console/app/server/actions/privacy and nothing there enforces them; the rest of the tree was not searched for those.

evidence.shows: The self-service privacy actions open an erasure case and do not build an export.
The case actions do not build an export either.

findings.quote: {CURRENT_LEGAL_OPERATOR} is not yet registered for VAT, so we do not currently take payment from individuals in any country.
findings.says: The page gives the missing VAT registration as the reason no individual can pay.
findings.actually: No individual can pay because PAID_MARKETS is empty, which is what the page's own condition reads. The tax research found that a VAT registration is not a precondition for selling to buyers in Bulgaria, nor to individuals elsewhere in the EU while those sales stay at or under EUR 10,000 a year. The stated reason is therefore not the real one, and it will read as false the day a consumer cell opens with the company still unregistered.

evidence.shows: No market is open, for either kind of buyer.

evidence.pattern: \| Bulgaria \| Business or individual \| \*\*May open with no registration \[C\]\*\*
evidence.shows: The tax research's verdict for Bulgaria.

findings.quote: Removed cloud inventory and capability observations: 7 days by default.
findings.says: The page publishes a 7-day window for removed inventory and capability observations.
findings.actually: The window is real (see the claim privacy.retention.removed-inventory), but the retention register has no entry for it, although that file states that nothing may be retained without appearing there. Its test covers only the gc_* SQL functions, and this purge is TypeScript, so nothing reports the gap. Not a false statement on the page; a hole in the register LEG-L4's retention schedule is to agree with.

evidence.shows: The retention register does not mention inventory.

evidence.pattern: nothing may be retained by this product\s*//\s*without appearing here
evidence.shows: The register's own statement of completeness.

findings.quote: Art. 97a(1) imposes the same registration on a company that **receives**
findings.says: Flagged by the tax research (1 of 3). The decisions of 2026-11-17 record that a Bulgarian company needs the Art. 97a registration before its first sale to a business in another member state.
findings.actually: Correct but incomplete. The same registration is triggered by receiving a taxable service from a supplier outside Bulgaria, whether or not anything has been sold, so it may already be due; the repository cannot see the purchase invoices that decide it. The dividing line is also not organization against consumer, as PayerCapacity draws it, but whether the customer has given a VAT number.

findings.quote: "No VAT registration now" and "EU businesses" do not fit together
findings.says: Flagged by the tax research (2 of 3). The decisions of 2026-11-17 open the EU to businesses and individuals with no VAT registration now, registering on traction.
findings.actually: The two cannot both hold for a business in another member state that gives a VAT number: the Art. 97a application is due seven days before that customer is first charged, so registering once there is a customer is too late. Either the registration is filed before launch or those cells stay closed.

findings.says: Flagged by the tax research (3 of 3). The paid-markets record lists what a consumer cell needs: pre-contractual information, the payment-obligation button, the 14-day withdrawal right, durable confirmation and dispute-body information.
findings.actually: It does not list the online withdrawal function that the Consumer Rights Directive has required since 19 June 2026 (Art. 11a; Bulgarian Consumer Protection Act Art. 52a, in force 24 September 2026): a control labelled "withdraw from contract here", a confirmation step, and an acknowledgement on a durable medium. Whether the console's withdrawal flow meets those labels was not checked here.

evidence.shows: The paid-markets record does not mention the function or either article.
The tax research says so.

findings.quote: Without an OSS registration there is no return through which to report VAT collected in another member state
findings.says: The tax condition says a sale to an individual elsewhere in the EU is taxed where the customer is and needs an OSS registration to report it.
findings.actually: The tax research found that this holds only above EUR 10,000 a year of such sales across the EU. At or under that total the place of supply stays in Bulgaria, an unregistered company charges no VAT on the sale, and no OSS registration is needed. Follows from the tax research; not one of the three points it raises itself.

evidence.pattern: No OSS registration is needed, and none is possible on these facts
evidence.shows: The tax research's conclusion below the threshold.
